goal: Add bounded autonomous input discovery, evidence-fitness ranking, retry, full analysis and video execution, and truthful synthetic fallback to the generated CS demo project.
acceptance_criteria: A failed candidate is recorded and the next ranked candidate is attempted automatically.
An auto-test CLI command discovers bounded local JSON, DEM, and safe ZIP candidates without crawling arbitrary locations.
Candidates are ranked using parseability, tick coverage, players, view angles, shots, visibility, information state, rounds, and map metadata.
The autonomous report redacts secrets, distinguishes discovery, execution, and evidence truth, and automated plus real CLI tests pass before local_packager rebuilds the bundle.
The selected authorized real input runs the existing eight-stage pipeline and the existing evidence-video renderer without adding a generation or delivery route.
When no authorized real input succeeds, an explicitly enabled deterministic synthetic fallback runs the same workflow and is reported as PASS_WITH_LIMITS rather than a real-demo success.

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

feedback: All 69 generated-project tests were collected: 68 passed, 0 failed, and 1 Windows symlink test was explicitly skipped; canonical test/runtime/visual/media/package inspections passed.
Authorized production DEM acquisition, demoparser2 compatibility, and calibrated detection rates remain outside this increment.

The project autonomously selected the only bundled candidate at fitness 81.25, completed analysis and a valid 4-second video, and correctly reported PASS_WITH_LIMITS because the selected input declares itself synthetic.
The final persistence probe confirmed that the real authorization assertion is used for acquisition but does not appear in the autonomous report, downstream acquisition manifest, or video sidecar.

worked: A thin librarian-style orchestration layer reused acquisition, parsing, analysis, and video interfaces without adding another generation or delivery route.
Actual failure injection proved that a high-score candidate can fail during video rendering and the workflow records the failure, cleans up FFmpeg, and selects the next candidate.
did_not_work: Static inspection exposed an existing CLI error-path NameError and rendering exceptions exposed missing FFmpeg cleanup.
The first autonomous run classified an externally stored synthetic fixture as if it represented a real match; source provenance and content truth needed separate fields.

The first privacy review checked only the top-level autonomous report; the reused pipeline also required a non-sensitive authorization receipt so environment-provided authorization text would not be persisted downstream.
experiments: Keep candidate context as scored receipts and attempt summaries; only load one selected input into the full pipeline, and record content truth independently from source type.
